strategy: Black-box equivalence/boundary design for the room-creation HTTP interface. The interface is fixed by REQ-001: POST /rooms submitted as player-a with a JSON body containing maxPlayers, mode, and ranked. REQ-002 fixes mode=duel and ranked=false for all requests in this task, so maxPlayers is the only varying input. The task declares exactly four independent tests, which map one-to-one to four scenarios: two values with a specified success outcome (maxPlayers=2 -> 201, maxPlayers=8 -> 201) and two boundary-adjacent values with a specified rejection outcome (maxPlayers=1 -> 400, maxPlayers=9 -> 400). Each scenario pairs the varying maxPlayers value with the fixed non-varying inputs, the declared endpoint/player/body shape, and the test-isolation precondition from REQ-007 (fresh framework fixture, no room shared between tests), so no state carries over and each test exercises room creation from a clean baseline. Expected results are only the explicitly declared HTTP status codes; no response fields, error body, authentication behavior, missing-field handling, concurrency behavior, or dependency-fault behavior is asserted because the source excludes them from this task's scope. Factors capture the endpoint contract, the fixed inputs, each declared maxPlayers value with its specified status, and the fixture-isolation precondition; every factor's sourceQuote is copied exactly from its linked requirement's quote. All in-scope expectations are specified and covered by the four declared tests, so no questions or gaps remain; excluded areas are recorded as scope limits, not gaps, and no execution or coverage beyond the declared scope is claimed.
